finding: The 'fetched_utc' timestamps in these registers cannot be real fetch times: several are later than the commit that added the file to main, and several are in the future relative to this review. A timestamp is a claim like any other and none of these can be reproduced.

where: root: 89 HTML files, 4 dashboard pages, 7 docs pages, 15 CI workflows
finding: Fourteen earlier layers each published their own cost table from their own rate snapshot, with four different headline figures for the same $10,000 conversion: $53.38, $53.42, $53.47 and $901.30 at $400,000 against $899.01. A reader landing on an archived page cannot tell which reading is current.

finding: The card said the currency gain is 'taxed at your ordinary rate unless the personal-transaction rule applies'. Read properly, §988(e)(2) gives relief only where the gain is USD 200 or less, so for any balance in this brief the rule cannot apply. The old wording invited the reader to hope otherwise.
action: Corrected in this release: the $200 limit is stated explicitly on the home, tax and costs pages.

finding: Every rate-based figure was computed from a single intraday Board of China snapshot, but none of the published pages measured how much of the headline is the snapshot rather than the channel. The movement between two readings of the same board on successive days (see the scenario rows below) is of the same order as some of the differences the layers argued about.
evidence: BOC board page read on 2026-11-10 17:39:58 (ask 6.69) and again on 2026-11-11 10:25:02 (ask 6.69): the same page moved by about 0.006 CNY per USD, which on $10,000 is about 5 cents of cost. S01.
action: This release adds a scenario table (A/B/C) holding the channel fixed and moving only the clock.

finding: The board grew to 1,298 lines of append-only session logs. action: Recorded once here rather than again per session. The rule should say 'one branch per session, named by the harness'.

finding: There are 15 CI workflows and 15 local validators, several of which re-implement the same arithmetic independently. That is good for catching errors, but four of them only assert internal consistency against their own data module, so they cannot detect a wrong input that is consistently applied. Passing 15 validators is not evidence that a figure is true.
evidence: scripts/verify_*.py: verify_completion.py restates a rate; verify_c3x_site.py imports its own inputs; neither fetches anything.
action: This release separates the two questions: the validators prove internal consistency, and the source register (data/r11_sources.csv) with a dated quote proves provenance. Both are printed on the sources page.
